newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Lagos sets up neighbourhood watch to fight crime.
newsitem.headline: Lagos sets up neighbourhood watch to fight crime.

text.p: A 3,000-strong neighbourhood watch group to help combat soaring crime in Nigeria's commercial hub of Lagos was set up on Friday, the state military chief said.
The News Agency of Nigeria reported that Colonel Mohammed Marwa told a security meeting with traditional rulers that the neighbourhood watch group would complement police efforts.
In July, Marwa's predecessor launched a similar group code-named "Operation Sweep", which is made up of the police and soldiers.
Residents say the operation has temporarily reduced armed robbery, a common thing in Lagos and other urban centres of impoverished Nigeria.
"I think the operation has tamed armed robbery somewhat but not totally eliminated the cause which is poverty," said Ishola Jimoh, a Lagos lawyer.
